paper.title: Efficient Pre-Training with Token Superposition
paper.summary: Token-Superposition Training combines contiguous tokens into bags, trains on averaged embeddings with a multi-hot cross-entropy objective, then recovers with standard next-token training. The paper reports robust throughput/loss gains from 270M through 10B A1B scale.

candidates.title: GPT-2 Scale Token-Superposition Pretraining Reproduction

source_records.title: Efficient Pre-Training with Token Superposition
source_records.summary: Token-Superposition Training uses a superposition phase over contiguous token bags with multi-hot cross entropy followed by recovery with standard next-token training.

candidates.hypothesis: A GPT-2-small-class local model can reproduce the paper's token-superposition training speed/quality tradeoff at small scale when compared under equal FLOPs and equal wall-clock budgets.
candidates.mechanism: Group contiguous tokens into bags, average their token embeddings into a shorter latent sequence, optimize multi-hot cross entropy over bag contents during a superposition phase, then switch to ordinary causal next-token pretraining for recovery.
candidates.description: Bounded reproduction of Token-Superposition Training on a GPT-2-scale model and public small corpus to determine whether the mechanism survives home-scale training.
candidates.implementation: Train a GPT-2-small or smaller decoder on TinyStories/FineWeb-Edu slice with baseline causal LM and TST s=2/s=4 variants. Match optimizer, tokens, FLOPs proxy, and wall-clock budget. Run recovery phase from the TST checkpoint. Save learning curves, throughput, final validation loss, and downstream small evals.
candidates.baseline_to_beat: Standard causal LM pretraining under matched wall-clock and matched update/FLOP proxy budgets.
candidates.success_threshold: TST reaches equal validation loss at >=1.25x lower wall-clock or reaches >=1% lower validation loss at the same wall-clock budget without downstream degradation beyond 2%.There must be at least two seeds or a clear deterministic small-run reproducibility check.
candidates.kill_condition: Stop if recovery fails to close within 2% validation loss of baseline, if throughput gain is below 1.10x after overhead, or if downstream evals regress by more than 3% at equal wall-clock.
candidates.accessibility_delta: If reproduced locally, TST could make home-scale pretraining experiments cheaper by trading a short recovery phase for higher data throughput.
likely_failure_modes: speedup erased by data packing overhead
downstream tasks suffer from order loss
candidates.novelty_comparison: This is not a new method claim; it is a targeted small-scale reproduction of a very recent pretraining-efficiency paper under local hardware constraints.
candidates.risk_notes: Small models and small corpora may not show the same scaling behavior as the paper's larger runs. Treat negative evidence as scale-limited unless implementation checks pass.

candidates.title: Annealed Recovery Schedule for Token-Superposition Training

source_records.title: Efficient Pre-Training with Token Superposition
source_records.summary: TST uses a superposition phase and then reverts to standard training for recovery.

candidates.hypothesis: Gradually annealing from multi-hot bag prediction to standard next-token cross entropy recovers ordering information faster than an abrupt objective switch after TST pretraining.
candidates.mechanism: During recovery, mix the TST multi-hot objective and next-token CE with a scheduled coefficient while reducing bag size or mask ambiguity over time, instead of switching objectives in one step.
candidates.description: Extension test for whether the recovery phase can be improved with an annealed or blended objective.
candidates.implementation: Start from identical TST checkpoints and compare abrupt CE recovery, linear MCE-to-CE anneal, cosine anneal, and bag-size shrink s=4-to-s=2-to-1. Measure recovery steps to baseline loss, final loss, downstream evals, and overhead.
candidates.baseline_to_beat: The original abrupt switch from TST superposition phase to standard causal next-token recovery.
candidates.success_threshold: Annealed recovery reaches baseline validation loss at least 15% faster than abrupt recovery or improves final validation loss by >=0.5% at matched recovery budget with no downstream degradation.
candidates.kill_condition: Stop if annealing changes recovery speed by less than 5%, introduces instability, or requires more hyperparameter tuning than the bounded schedule sweep allows.
candidates.accessibility_delta: A better recovery schedule would make TST more practical for local users by reducing the expensive standard-training tail.
likely_failure_modes: anneal schedule has no measurable effect
candidates.novelty_comparison: Extends the paper by targeting a likely improvement point: the transition from unordered bag prediction back to ordered causal prediction.
candidates.risk_notes: If the paper already tuned recovery strongly, a simple anneal may not beat it. Keep schedule count bounded and compare from the same checkpoint.

candidates.title: Position-Weighted Multi-Hot Objective for Token Superposition

source_records.title: Efficient Pre-Training with Token Superposition
source_records.summary: TST trains a multi-hot objective over tokens contained in each superposed bag.

candidates.hypothesis: A position- or rarity-weighted multi-hot objective preserves more recoverable order and information than uniform multi-hot prediction while retaining most TST throughput benefits.
candidates.mechanism: Assign nonuniform target weights inside each superposed bag using recency, token rarity, or boundary markers, so the model learns a weak ordering prior instead of a pure unordered set objective.
candidates.description: Objective-level extension of TST that tests whether some order signal can be retained without returning to full-length causal training.
candidates.implementation: Implement uniform MCE, position-weighted MCE, inverse-frequency weighted MCE, and boundary-emphasized MCE on the same TST setup. Compare loss, recovery speed, downstream evals, and throughput overhead against uniform TST.
candidates.baseline_to_beat: Uniform multi-hot cross entropy TST at the same bag size and recovery budget.
candidates.success_threshold: Weighted MCE improves recovery speed by >=10% or final validation loss by >=0.5% versus uniform MCE while preserving at least 90% of the measured TST throughput gain.
candidates.kill_condition: Stop if weighted targets reduce throughput below 90% of uniform TST, fail to improve recovery, or overfit token-frequency artifacts.
candidates.accessibility_delta: If successful, local training runs could recover quality faster without changing model architecture or tokenizer.
candidates.novelty_comparison: Applies a simple information-preservation modification to the paper's bag objective rather than only reproducing the original method.
candidates.risk_notes: Small gains could be noise; require shared seeds and identical packing to avoid false positives.

candidates.title: Adaptive Bag-Size Curriculum for Token-Superposition Training

source_records.title: Efficient Pre-Training with Token Superposition
source_records.summary: TST combines many contiguous tokens into one bag, creating a bag-size tradeoff between throughput and order information loss.

candidates.hypothesis: A curriculum that starts with large token-superposition bags and shrinks bag size before recovery gives a better throughput-quality Pareto point than any fixed bag size.
candidates.mechanism: Use large bags early for maximum data throughput, then progressively reduce bag size as model loss falls so later training carries more order information before standard recovery.
candidates.description: Tests a curriculum variant of TST that treats bag size as a schedule rather than a fixed pretraining hyperparameter.
candidates.implementation: Compare fixed s=2, fixed s=4, fixed s=8 if feasible, and curricula s=8->4->2 and s=4->2 on the same token and wall-clock budgets. Use identical recovery length and log throughput/quality tradeoffs.
candidates.baseline_to_beat: Best fixed-bag TST variant under the same total wall-clock budget.
candidates.success_threshold: Adaptive bag-size curriculum improves final validation loss by >=0.75% versus best fixed-bag TST or reaches equal loss with >=10% lower wall-clock.
candidates.kill_condition: Stop if curriculum does not beat the best fixed bag size after the first bounded sweep or if large-bag startup causes unrecoverable loss spikes.
candidates.accessibility_delta: A curriculum could make TST easier to tune locally by exposing a simple schedule with better quality-throughput tradeoff.
likely_failure_modes: large bag size erases too much order
schedule benefit is just longer effective recovery
candidates.novelty_comparison: Turns TST bag size into a training curriculum, an adjacent but distinct intervention from a fixed superposition phase.
candidates.risk_notes: Needs strict accounting so curriculum does not accidentally receive more effective ordered training than the fixed baseline.

candidates.title: Token Superposition for Long-Context Anchor Compression

source_records.title: Efficient Pre-Training with Token Superposition
source_records.summary: TST compresses contiguous tokens into averaged embeddings and predicts bag contents with a multi-hot objective.

candidates.hypothesis: The token-superposition idea can be repurposed as a long-context memory compressor: superposed span embeddings plus exact anchors preserve retrieval facts better than naive chunk averaging at the same memory budget.
candidates.mechanism: Represent non-anchor spans as averaged token-superposition embeddings while preserving exact named entities, numbers, and retrieval needles as anchors. Query-time retrieval combines dense superposed span similarity with exact anchor lookup.
candidates.description: Transplants the paper's superposition principle from pretraining throughput to long-context memory compression and anchor retrieval.
candidates.implementation: Build a synthetic 64K-256K retrieval benchmark with needles, named entities, and distractors. Compare exact chunk text RAG, mean embedding chunks, superposed span embeddings, and superposed spans plus exact anchors. Measure recall, memory bytes, latency, and hallucinated-anchor rate.
candidates.baseline_to_beat: Vector-RAG chunk embeddings and periodic exact-anchor baselines at the same memory footprint.
candidates.success_threshold: Superposed spans plus anchors improve multi-needle retrieval accuracy by >=10 percentage points versus mean chunk embeddings at <=50% of exact text storage, with hallucinated-anchor rate below 2%.
candidates.kill_condition: Stop if superposed span retrieval is not better than mean embedding chunks, if exact anchors explain all gains, or if memory footprint exceeds the configured budget.
candidates.accessibility_delta: If useful, home systems could store longer histories with less memory while preserving exact facts that should not be compressed away.
likely_failure_modes: retrieval gains vanish on multi-hop queries
candidates.novelty_comparison: Applies token superposition outside pretraining, using it as a compressed long-context memory representation rather than a training throughput method.
candidates.risk_notes: This is a transplant idea, not direct validation of the paper. It should be treated as a branch only after basic TST reproduction candidates are considered.
